title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
description: Discover the specific study nooks, quiet courtyards, and rooftop terraces that Auburn students use for daily productivity and relaxation beyond the standard landmark stops.

cards.title: The Deep Quiet Zone
cards.subtitle: Ralph Brown Draughon Library
cards.notes: Head to the top floor for strictly enforced individual quiet study. It is the campus standard for distraction-free finals prep.
cards.short_summary: The designated silent floor of Auburn's main library, preferred for intense individual focus.
cards.evidence_claim: The entire 4th floor of the Ralph Brown Draughon (RBD) Library is officially designated as a quiet study area.
cards.source_title: Are there any quiet study areas in the library? - LibAnswers
cards.access_notes: Open to students during library operating hours; Tiger Card required for late-night entry.

cards.title: Mell Street Collaboration Hub
cards.subtitle: Mell Classroom Building
cards.notes: Use the glass-enclosed 'collaboratories' for group projects. These rooms feature integrated tech and whiteboards for team sessions.
cards.short_summary: High-tech group study rooms located in the Mell Classroom Building adjacent to the main library.
cards.evidence_claim: The Mell Classroom Building features 'collaboratories' and glass-enclosed study rooms designed for group work and interactive education.
cards.source_title: Auburn University Mell Classroom Building @ RBD Library - AIA Georgia
cards.access_notes: Rooms can be reserved by students via the Skedda system using an AU email.

cards.title: The 16-Acre Outdoor Classroom
cards.subtitle: Garden Drive
cards.notes: Walk the shaded trails to find quiet benches for reading. It is a primary spot for students to escape the noise of College Street.
cards.short_summary: A serene botanical garden on campus used by students for nature walks and quiet reflection.
cards.evidence_claim: The Davis Arboretum is a 16-acre botanic garden open daily from sunrise to sunset with no admission charge.
cards.source_title: Donald E. Davis Arboretum | College of Sciences and Mathematics
cards.access_notes: Open daily from sunrise to sunset; free and open to the public.

cards.title: Stadium View Study Spot
cards.subtitle: Horton-Hardgrave Hall
cards.notes: Visit the 4th-floor rooftop for covered outdoor seating and views of Jordan-Hare Stadium. It is a favorite for open-air studying.
cards.short_summary: A rooftop terrace in the business complex offering collaborative spaces and campus views.
cards.evidence_claim: The Gavin Terrace on the 4th floor of Horton-Hardgrave Hall offers covered seating and views of Jordan-Hare Stadium.
cards.source_title: Auburn offers popular study spots and helpful study tips as semester finals near
cards.access_notes: Accessible to students during building hours; features flexible and convertible spaces.

cards.title: The Campus Family Room
cards.subtitle: Heisman Drive
cards.notes: Utilize the upper-floor lounges for a mix of social and quiet space. The building also houses the Foy Information Desk for any campus questions.
cards.short_summary: The central hub for student life, offering various lounges, dining, and meeting spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: The Harold D. Melton Student Center provides 184,000 square feet of space for student meeting rooms, study areas, and lounges.
cards.source_title: AU Facilities Management - Melton Student Center Building Profile
cards.access_notes: Open daily; hours vary by semester but typically include late-night access.

cards.title: The Design School Courtyard
cards.subtitle: Dudley Hall
cards.notes: Relax in 'The Grove' section of the courtyard, which features moveable chairs and a shady canopy of trees near the architecture studios.
cards.short_summary: A renovated series of outdoor spaces including a theater forecourt and a shaded grove.
cards.evidence_claim: The Dudley Yards include 'The Grove,' a courtyard space with a shady grove of trees and moveable chairs.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor public space accessible to all students.

cards.title: Artistic Study Escape
cards.subtitle: South College Street
cards.notes: Spread out on the museum grounds or use the lobby's modular couches for reading. The walking path is exactly one mile for three loops.
cards.short_summary: The university's fine art museum offering quiet indoor and outdoor spaces for students.
cards.evidence_claim: The Jule Collins Smith Museum of Fine Art offers free admission and grounds with landscaped walking paths and sculptures.
cards.source_title: Auburn offers popular study spots and helpful study tips as semester finals near
cards.access_notes: Admission is free; Tiger Transit runs to this location on the South Quad-Fine Arts Line.

cards.title: The Business Hub
cards.subtitle: Lowder Hall Ground Floor
cards.notes: Find the student study area in room 023 on the ground floor. It is conveniently located near the building's Starbucks for quick breaks.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated study area within the Harbert College of Business complex.
cards.evidence_claim: Lowder Hall's ground floor includes a designated student study area in room 023.
cards.source_title: Harbert College of Business Locations - Auburn University
cards.access_notes: Open during business school operating hours; team rooms require reservation via Mazévo.

cards.title: Modern Lab Complex Nooks
cards.subtitle: Academic Classroom and Laboratory Complex
cards.notes: Look for the relaxation and quiet study areas tucked between the labs. This new facility offers some of the most modern furniture on campus.
cards.short_summary: Quiet study and relaxation zones within the new ACLC building near the campus amphitheater.
cards.evidence_claim: The Academic Classroom and Laboratory Complex (ACLC) features adaptable classroom spaces and quiet study areas.
cards.source_title: Auburn offers popular study spots and helpful study tips as semester finals near
cards.access_notes: Open to students during academic building hours.

cards.entity_name: Walt and Ginger Woltosz Rooftop Terrace
cards.title: The Culinary View
cards.subtitle: Tony and Libba Rane Culinary Science Center
cards.notes: Access this terrace before 3 p.m. for a quiet study spot with garden spaces and views of Samford Hall.
cards.short_summary: A rooftop garden terrace that serves as a student study spot during daytime hours.
cards.evidence_claim: The rooftop terrace at the Rane Culinary Science Center is open to students for study until 3 p.m. each day.
cards.source_title: Find out where students are studying this fall - Auburn University
cards.access_notes: Open to students until 3:00 PM daily before transitioning to a commercial venue.
